OGS-00009 rebuilt against OGS-00010

The 0.2.0 ukb-b Reference-Completed Store against the 0.1.0 one it replaces · size, structure, query time, MR controls, regions and observed-cell fidelity

Published

October 24, 2026

ImportantWhat changed, and the headline numbers

The rebuilt OGS-00009 replaces OGS-00010. They are both Reference-Completed UK Biobank ukb-b Dense Stores, and they differ in five independent ways. Every section below says which of the five it measures:

  1. Membership: 490 Analyses added, 0 removed (2,514 against 2,024).
  2. Completion panel: the UKB EUR LD panel (ukb-hg38-eur-ld) (9,847,807 panel variants) against the HGDP+1kGP hg38 EUR panel (9,782,961).
  3. hg19 lift: opengwas/opengwasdb#288 projects reverse-strand variants onto the hg38 strand, which renames 9,420 observed variants and re-orients 1,861 reverse-strand palindromes.
  4. Format: 0.2.0 (Zarr v3, inner chunk [1000, 64], shard [100000, 1024]) against 0.1.0 (Zarr v2, [1000, 1000] chunks).
  5. Identity model: single-id (store_id OGS-00009, release_id OGS-00009-completed) against a two-id child (store_id OGS-00009, release_id OGS-00010).
  • Build collisions, both Stores: 8 rows × 2,514 Analyses (20,112 cells, 16,818 observed) in the new OGS-00009, and 5 rows × 2,024 Analyses (10,120 cells, 8,864 observed) in the old OGS-00010, hold one of two colliding source variants’ statistics (opengwas/opengwasdb#325). See Build collisions.
  • Size: 64.69 GB against 49.33 GB (1.31x), 2.299 against 1.799 bytes per cell. The new Store holds 28.13 bn cells against 27.43 bn, and fewer of them are empty.
  • Query time (median of 7 warm calls): one Analysis genome-wide, observed cells only, takes 7.76 s (7,578,648 results) against 26.79 s (7,578,651 results). With all of each Store’s own cells, it takes 8.15 s (9,975,895 results) against 27.23 s (11,229,918 results). A PheWAS over the shared Analyses takes 31.5 ms (2,024 results) against 30.9 ms (2,020 results).
  • MR, observed-only variants: 3 of 3 positive controls keep their sign and their significance across the Stores: bmi_chd +0.0132 (591 instruments) against +0.0132 (591), agreeing to 5 significant figures; ldl_chd +0.1497 (34 instruments) against +0.1497 (34), agreeing to 5 significant figures; smoking_lung -0.0016 (54 instruments) against -0.0016 (54), agreeing to 4 significant figures.
  • Observed-cell fidelity, by ALID over the 2,024 shared Analyses, in two strata that overlap:
    • 579,763,142 old observed cells at 500,004 variants in seeded windows (5.1% of the observed axis);
    • 14,190,874 cells at every observed variant the lift could have touched and at every build-collision row.
    0 cells are unexplained in either stratum. That holds beside the cells at build collisions (d): 18,120 in the second stratum (1,967 of them also fall in the windows). In the second stratum, 2,214,318 cells are re-oriented by opengwas/opengwasdb#288 (a), and 11,270,573 sit under a variant that only one Store spells that way (b).

WarningThe manifest cannot say which panel completed a Store

Both manifests record ld_panel_id as eur-hg38-gpm, but the two Stores were completed against different panels. The identifier is a constant in the completion code, and complete-dense has no flag that sets it. The only provenance that tells the panels apart is the completion step record (records/complete.json: its argv and its LD panel: line), and that is where the table above reads them from.

new OGS-00009’s parent is the observed-only release it was completed from (/data/opengwasdb/stores/OGS-00009/replaced/20261023T190459Z/store.opengwasdb). old OGS-00010’s parent is the old OGS-00009 (/data/opengwasdb/stores/OGS-00009/replaced/20261021T223815Z/store.opengwasdb). Each parent’s variant table is that Store’s observed axis, and the fidelity and regional sections use it to separate observed variants from the panel-only rows that completion added. The package version and a Store Release’s format_version are different things and move independently.

Reading the size difference. Of the new Store’s 64.69 GB, 8.20 GB is the HM3 Indexed Variant Subset. That is a derived query index (ADR 0061) the old Store does not carry. Without it the Stores are 56.49 GB against 49.33 GB. Three things make up that difference.

  • Content. The new Store has 1.03x the cells (2,514 Analyses on 11.19 M variants, against 2,024 on 13.55 M). Its panel adds 1.34 M rows where the old one added 3.70 M, and fewer of its cells are empty: off-panel cells are 9.8% of the grid against 19.7%. An empty cell compresses to almost nothing, so a fuller grid costs more bytes per cell.
  • Format. This comparison cannot isolate the format, because no other variable is held fixed. opengwas/opengwasdb#246 did isolate it: the same old observed OGS-00009 data, converted rather than rebuilt, took 34.68 GB in the 0.1.0 shape and 35.17 GB in the adopted 0.2.0 shape (1.014x; measured at 34b4ed1 on 2026-10-06). So the 0.2.0 layout itself accounts for about +1.4% of the size.
  • A codec setting. Neither content nor layout: an estimated 2.83 GB of the new Store, from 200 sampled chunks, is its SE plane’s Blosc typesize (next callout).

Of the 7.16 GB gap without HM3, then, an estimated 2.83 GB is the codec setting, roughly 0.68 GB is the layout, and the remaining ~3.65 GB is content.

WarningThe new OGS-00009’s se plane is compressed as if its cells were 4 bytes wide

se is int8 (1 byte per cell), but its Blosc codec records typesize: 4. Zarr v3 stores the typesize and Blosc bit-shuffles by it, so the bits of 4 neighbouring cells are interleaved rather than each cell’s own. Re-encoding 200 seeded inner chunks with the stored codec’s parameters takes 1.51x the bytes at typesize 4 that it takes at typesize 1. Scaled by that ratio, the plane would be about 5.50 GB instead of 8.33 GB: an estimated 2.83 GB of this Store, from 200 sampled chunks, is the codec setting. The values decode correctly; only the size is affected.

The cause is in the writer, not this Store. opengwasdb.encoding.se._rewrite_arrays creates the int8 SE plane, and its exception tables, with compressor_of(source): the codec of the float32 scratch plane it replaces, whose typesize zarr has already fixed at 4. Zarr v2 took the typesize from the buffer at encode time, so 0.1.0 Stores never showed this, and any 0.2.0 Dense Store with residual-coded SE written this way will.

Structure: format 0.2.0 against 0.1.0

Every Zarr array in each Store, read back from its own metadata (compare_store_releases.discover_arrays). A 0.1.0 array is Zarr v2 with one Blosc compressor and no shard. A 0.2.0 array is Zarr v3 whose Blosc codec sits inside sharding_indexed: the inner chunk is the read unit and the shard is the file.

Query time

Both Stores were timed by the generic store-comparison harness (benchmarks/benchmark_store_comparison.py), the same instrument opengwas/opengwasdb#240 and opengwas/opengwasdb#246 measured with. The selection was resolved once, before either Store was timed. It is recorded in opengwasdb_ogs00009_vs_ogs00010_queries.json under selection; that file’s sha256 is 9cedc30b21fb….

  • The exposure is statin use (ukb-b-17805), and the PheWAS variant is 19:44908822:C:T (APOE).
  • The region is chr19:44.5–45.5 Mb, using only the 3,989 ALIDs both axes carry.
  • The 100 random variants are drawn from the 10,740,157 ALIDs on both axes. The 100 random Analyses are drawn from the 2,024 shared Analyses.

Not every shape is the same query on both Stores.

  • bulk reads one Analysis on each Store’s own axis: 9,975,895 against 11,229,918 results.
  • tophits reads each Store’s own genome-wide hits: 2,960 against 3,488.
  • Their observed-only twins nearly match: 7,578,648 against 7,578,651, and 2,564 against 2,564. They are the like-for-like timings.
  • phewas and regional keep their historical meaning: every Analysis a Store holds. They therefore return wider results on the new Store. Their _shared_analyses and _shared twins ask both Stores the same question.

The harness times one Store’s column, then the next. Each column waited for the 1-minute load to fall below 48.0 before starting (the node has 224 cores and is shared with other builds), and every shape records the load average before and after it. Blosc decodes with 8 threads through zarr’s FusedCodecPipeline at max_workers=1, the package’s pinned reader. warm page cache: the node holds about 1 TB of page cache and the stores are warm. A cold-cache run cannot be forced without root, so these timings are warm-cache numbers, not first-touch disk numbers.

What to make of the timings. The format moves them most. The 1000×64 inner chunk makes one-Analysis reads over many variants (bulk, regional_one_analysis) much cheaper. Random lookups, and reads across every Analysis (phewas, regional), pay for more chunks. The indexed top-hit reads are close in both Stores. opengwas/opengwasdb#246 measured that effect on identical data; the same seven shapes are reproduced here from its artifact, so the format effect can be read without the content change:

HM3 extraction

The new Store publishes the HM3 Indexed Variant Subset (1,206,088 variants; 1,206,088 of 1,206,903 requested ALIDs resolved). Extracting ukb-b-17805 from it takes 469.8 ms (first call 450.0 ms, 1,193,015 cells), against 8.15 s for the whole Analysis genome-wide. The old Store has none (status missing: no Indexed Variant Subset named ‘hm3’ is published).

MR positive controls

Each pair runs on each Store under three conditions:

  • all: every instrument and outcome cell the Store holds;
  • observed: observed_only=True throughout;
  • imputed: instruments imputed in both the exposure and the outcome.

The method is unchanged from the OGS-00010 report: p < 5e-8, greedy 1 Mb pruning, then IVW. Observed-only estimates measure the lift and the membership, not the panel, and should agree. All and imputed estimates also carry the panel.

ukb-b has no LDL biomarker, so the “LDL” exposure is statin use, which is confounded by indication. It also has no lung-cancer incidence trait: the outcome is the ICD-10 C34.1 cancer-site field, which is coded only among cancer cases, so it is a collider endpoint. These pairs check the pipeline and the Stores against each other. They are not causal estimates.

Build collisions

When the hg19 → hg38 lift puts two source variants on one ALID, build-dense-vcf writes both into that ALID’s row. The row keeps one rsid and one source’s statistics, and its source_alid is blanked as ambiguous. Nothing fails: validate and the observed-view check both pass (opengwas/opengwasdb#325).

This section reads each Store on its own, because a collision both Stores share is invisible to any comparison between them.

  • Rows are the blank source_alids of the Store’s observed-only parent, each confirmed on the published completed axis under the same rsid.
  • Sources are the source GWAS-VCF’s records that the Store’s own lift puts on the ALID.
  • Whose statistics the row holds is decided by comparing the stored z with each source’s z, in ukb-b-17805 and ukb-b-19953.

The class predates opengwas/opengwasdb#288. Of the new Store’s 8 collisions, 5 are carried over from the old Store and 3 are new: opengwas/opengwasdb#288’s complement lands a renamed reverse-strand variant on an ALID another source already holds. 3 of the 3 new ones sit at an ALID the old Store held uncollided, so a lookup that used to return that variant’s own association now returns another variant’s: 7:74988062:G:T was rs35525401 and now holds 7:74844193:C:A’s statistics under rs35525401; 7:75044656:A:C was rs587647277 and now holds 7:74787650:G:T’s statistics under rs587647277; 7:101668260:A:G was rs848673 and now holds 19:7323129:T:C’s statistics under rs200217321. 0 of the old Store’s collisions are gone. Every row holds exactly one source’s statistics: a lookup returns that source’s association at the position, and the other source’s is lost. The cross-Store view of the 3 new collisions (lift_axis.collapsed) points here.

Observed-cell fidelity

This section asks whether the two Stores hold the same observed cells. A cell is an Analysis × variant pair, matched by ALID, over the 2,024 shared Analyses. Every observed cell of the old Store gets exactly one category:

  • identical: z bit-identical; SE and EAF within the encoding’s tolerance (below).
  • (a) re-oriented by opengwas/opengwasdb#288: a palindromic SNP the chain lifts through a reverse-strand block, decided from the chain alone. Its ALID is unchanged, z is exactly negated, EAF becomes 1 − EAF, and SE is unchanged.
  • (b) present in only one Store: opengwas/opengwasdb#288 renamed the variant (its alleles complemented), and its cells reappear, re-oriented, under the new spelling.
  • (d) build collision: the row is a build collision in either Store, or lands on one, so it holds one of two sources’ statistics (opengwas/opengwasdb#325).
  • palindrome, strand ambiguous: a palindrome whose hg19 source the chain maps both ways. It is counted apart from (a), and only when one orientation holds.
  • (c) unexplained: anything else, including a variant that is gone with no lift evidence for why. Any cell here stops the benchmark run.

A new observed cell that no old cell accounts for is (d) at a collision row and (c) anywhere else.

The two observed axes were compared in full: every variant of each parent’s variant table. Which chain block each variant lies under is read from the hg19 → hg38 chain (hg19ToHg38.over.chain.gz, sha256 5c0598e500ce…).

  • A rename or a reverse-only palindrome counts as reproduced when the package’s own lifted_rows takes the old spelling, read back to hg19 through the reverse block, to the new spelling on the reverse strand.
  • A palindrome under blocks of both orientations is decided by lifting its hg19 source_alid (from the old parent) through the chain, never by which orientation its cells fit.

The run stops if any reproduction falls short, or if a variant only one Store carries lies outside every reverse-strand block.

“Of the (d) cells, reproduced by the other Store” counts the (d) cells whose counterpart in the new Store agrees with the old cell, re-oriented where the lift implies. It is informative, not a verdict. A collision both Stores share and resolve to the same source reproduces; a collision that keeps the other source in one Store does not, and nor does the cell of the source a collision dropped.

How large the sample is. The seeded stratum draws 1,000 non-overlapping windows of 500 consecutive old observed variants (seed 20261024), giving 500,004 variants. That is 5.1% of the old observed axis, and 579,763,142 observed cells across all 2,024 shared Analyses. Each window is read by position on both Stores, so a variant only one Store spells that way is inside it too. With none unexplained, the rule of three bounds the rate of variants carrying an unexplained difference below 6.0e-06 (95%). The second stratum is not a sample: it covers every observed variant the lift could have touched and every build-collision row of either Store.

Identical cells z bit-identical SE bit-identical EAF bit-identical max |Δ log SE| max |Δ logit EAF|
Seeded random windows 100.0% 11.4% 72.9% 0.003937 0.003942
Every observed variant the lift could touch, and every collision row 100.0% 14.0% 74.7% 0.003937 0.003953

Why SE and EAF are compared with a tolerance. z is int16_fixed, an exact code, so it is compared bit for bit and matches in every identical cell. SE and EAF are int8_residual: each Store codes a value as a residual against its own baseline, and the baselines move with membership. The EAF baseline is the median over a Store’s Analyses. So each Store decodes within half a quantisation step of the source value, and two Stores can differ by up to one step: 0.003938 in log SE and 0.003938 in logit EAF. A frequency also carries float32 rounding, which near 0 or 1 adds up to 2 * 2^-24 / min(f, 1 - f) to its logit. That matters for the rare variants the lift flipped close to 1. The widest gaps above sit right at that bound. Any real difference is far larger: a wrong orientation moves the logit by 2 |logit(f)|.

Caveats

  • Both Stores carry build collisions. 8 rows × 2,514 Analyses (20,112 cells, 16,818 observed) in the new OGS-00009, and 5 rows × 2,024 Analyses (10,120 cells, 8,864 observed) in the old OGS-00010, hold one of two colliding source variants’ statistics (opengwas/opengwasdb#325). A lookup of one of these rows returns one source’s association, often under the other source’s rsid, with no warning. The fidelity check counts their cells as (d), apart from (c). Its “0 unexplained” holds only beside them.
  • Imputed cells differ because the panels differ. UKB EUR LD against HGDP+1KGP EUR. The two Stores’ imputed values, panel rows, regional imputed points and the all- and imputed-condition MR estimates are not expected to agree, and no section treats a difference there as a defect. Only observed cells are held to identity.
  • Timings come from a shared host. The node runs other builds. Each Store’s column waited for the 1-minute load to fall below the gate, and every shape records its load average, but the columns ran one after the other, so a load change between them lands on one Store. The page cache is warm and uncontrolled: “first call” means the shape’s first call, not a cold disk read.
  • Format and content are not separated here. The new Store is bigger and differently shaped. The opengwas/opengwasdb#246 reference rows (the same data in both shapes) are where the format effect alone can be read.
  • The fidelity check is by ALID. It examines the shared Analyses only. The 490 added Analyses have no counterpart to compare.
  • The panel provenance comes from step records, not the manifest. See the warning under The two Stores.
  • Two MR pairs are proxies, as flagged above.

Lookup timings moved between this report’s runs, on the new Store only. PheWAS on the new Store took 25.0 ms in round 0 (backup/r0-bench-ogs00009-vs-ogs00010) and 45.3 ms in this run. The old Store went from 23.9 ms to 24.6 ms. The two runs’ warm ranges on the new Store do not overlap: 24.3 ms–27.4 ms against 43.0 ms–48.0 ms. So the within-run spread understates lookup-time uncertainty on a shared host. Read the medians below as one draw each.
